purpose: A lossless TXL shorter than ngspice's step stays an exact delay line: ESPice's 0.9 tau step bound, not ngspice's ratio path.

oracle.derivation: Z0 = sqrt(l/c) = 50 ohm, tau = sqrt(l c) length = 0.5 ns, 50 ohm at both ends, so v(out)(t) = 0.5 vs(t - tau) exactly (no reflection). vs = PULSE(0 1 0 2n 2n 10n 20n) gives the values at the sample times in the deck header. Each sample is at least 0.5 ns from a corner of v(out), so any grid with steps under 0.45 ns interpolates it exactly; what remains is ngspice-compatible 0.1 gmin port stamping (5e-12 V). atol 1e-5 V: the ratio path ngspice takes past tau (txlload.c:221-228) is 1.3e-4 V off at 13 ns and 6.4e-5 V at 13.5 ns.
oracle.cross_check: /nix/store/bywwgg84ccx0544z9qrfm4zc4ls30ghd-ngspice-44.2/bin/ngspice -b txl_tran_lossless_step_bound.sp (ngspice-45 prints the same lines): every sample equal to the closed form to 7 digits except o13 = 0.3751345 and o13_5 = 0.2500637, which this oracle rejects. The prebuilt espice of 2026-11-10, at r=0.01 (the same lossless branch; r enters only the operating point, which is 0 V), is within 5e-12 V of every value.
